name: Target Reconnaissance & OSINT
description: Ability to gather open-source intelligence on target organisations and individuals to support social engineering campaigns. Covers organisational mapping, employee profiling, social media analysis, metadata harvesting, and building target dossiers. Focused on the social engineering application of OSINT (target selection, email-format and pretext discovery, phishability assessment) rather than the broader intelligence discipline; general person, social media, and infrastructure research techniques are covered by INTEL-OSINT-PERSON, INTEL-OSINT-SOCIAL, and INTEL-OSINT-INFRA.

0.label: None
0.description: No exposure to OSINT or target reconnaissance for social engineering

1.label: Awareness
1.description: Understands OSINT sources and techniques relevant to social engineering
evidence: Can identify key open-source data sources (LinkedIn, company websites, SEC filings, social media)
Understands OPSEC considerations when conducting OSINT

2.label: Guided Practice
2.description: Performs basic target reconnaissance under supervision using standard tools and methods
evidence: Conducted OSINT gathering on target organisations in lab exercises
Used tools such as theHarvester, Maltego, or LinkedIn to map target personnel
Produced basic target profiles reviewed by senior staff

3.label: Independent Practice
3.description: Independently conducts comprehensive target reconnaissance supporting campaign design
evidence: Produced target dossiers used to design social engineering campaigns on 3+ engagements
Identified key targets, reporting structures, and communication patterns from open sources
Discovered pretextable information (events, projects, vendors) from OSINT
Conducted reconnaissance without alerting target (maintained OPSEC)

4.label: Advanced / Mentor
4.description: Conducts deep-dive reconnaissance against security-conscious targets; develops OSINT playbooks
evidence: Performed OSINT against targets with limited public exposure, finding actionable intelligence
Combined multiple OSINT sources to build comprehensive organisational maps
Developed automated OSINT collection workflows for the lab
Mentors team on OSINT methodology and tool usage

5.label: Expert / Authority
5.description: Defines OSINT methodology for social engineering; researches novel collection techniques
evidence: Authored the lab's OSINT methodology for social engineering reconnaissance
Developed novel OSINT collection techniques or tool integrations
Trains teams on advanced OSINT techniques and operational security
Recognised as the authority on target reconnaissance within the lab

assessment_methods.description: Given a target organisation name, produce a reconnaissance dossier within a defined time window, assessed on breadth, depth, actionability, and OPSEC
Review target dossiers and OSINT reports from recent engagements
